text:
maya_sales: Hey team, ACME POC stuck on onboarding. They say SCIM provisioning keeps 400ing when creating users from Okta. Need quick triage, POC demo on Friday.
jamie_se: Ugh ok. Any error payloads from Okta? usually the /scim/v2/Users post will include a JSON error we can share with eng.
maya_sales: Paste from ACME: `HTTP 400 Bad Request - {\"detail\":\"Invalid attribute mapping: 'title' not in schema\"}` They mapped email -> userName and included title/group membership.
anita_security: That looks like a schema mismatch. Our SCIM server expects `userName`, `name.givenName`, `name.familyName` and `emails[type=work].value`. Extra attrs should be ignored, not 400. Did they enable strict mode on their Okta SCIM app?
jamie_se: Good call. @acme-idp-admin (they're not in this channel) mentioned they used a custom mapper that only forwards a handful of attributes. Can we check our SCIM strictness flag for POC org acme-poc-432?
nathan_enginfra: I can look. For Dedicated and Hosted POC orgs we toggle `scim.strictValidation` per-tenant. Running quick check... deploy-bot: Provisioning action: Dedicated pool credential issued for tenant acme-poc-432 at 2026-03-20T14:22Z.
jamie_se: Thanks bot. @nathan_enginfra what's the current value?
nathan_enginfra: It was flipped to true during a security test last week. I'll set it to false for the POC until we fix mapping. Doing it now.
deploy-bot: config update: tenant=acme-poc-432 key=scim.strictValidation old=true new=false by nathan_enginfra
maya_sales: Will tell ACME to retry.
acme_admin (reported via email): Retried and now getting 403 Forbidden when hitting /scim/v2/Users with the token we gave them.
jamie_se: 403 usually means the API key scope or org mapping is wrong. Which key did we give them? Hosted API key vs Dedicated pool key matters for SCIM write perms.
nathan_enginfra: They were using the dedicated pool API key but it was for the worker pool not the control plane. For SCIM we require control-plane scoped token `scim:write` issued from the console. I'll generate a short-lived token and paste secure link.
deploy-bot: new token generated for tenant=acme-poc-432 scopes=[scim:read,scim:write] expires=2026-03-21T02:22Z — token link: https://redwood-internal/secret/xxxx (internal only)
maya_sales: Sent to ACME admin via secure channel.
acme_admin (via email): Now we get 401 Unauthorized with the new token.
jamie_se: 401 points to clock skew or wrong signing key. Are they hitting the right endpoint? We have two endpoints: Hosted control plane `https://api.redwood.ai/scim/v2` and Dedicated control plane `https://acme-poc-432-control.redwood.private/scim/v2` (private access requires VPN / VPC routing).
maya_sales: They were pointing at `https://dedicated.redwood.ai/scim/v2` per their notes.
nathan_enginfra: That endpoint is shared but requires the dedicated tenant header: `X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-poc-432`. If they omitted the header, token won't map.
jamie_se: Can you share a minimal request example we can give ACME?
nathan_enginfra: Sure, share this snippet:
```
POST /scim/v2/Users HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-poc-432
Content-Type: application/scim+json

{ "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"], "userName":"jdoe@example.com", "name": {"givenName":"John","familyName":"Doe"}, "emails": [{"value":"jdoe@example.com","type":"work"}] }
```
maya_sales: Sharing with ACME now.
acme_admin (email): They followed the request exactly but now Okta provisioning logs show `SAML assertion missing groups claim` — their rule expects groups to map to Okta Group Push.
anita_security: For SAML SSO we need the IdP to include the group claim if ACME wants auto-group assignment. Our SAML metadata currently requests `urn:oid:1.3.6.1.4.1.5923.1.1.1` (eduPersonEntitlement) for groups, but many IdPs send `groups` or `memberOf`. We can add alternate attribute mappings on the tenant config.
jamie_se: Is that a console change we can do quickly? I want to avoid them editing IdP config mid-demo.
nathan_enginfra: I can add group claim fallbacks: accept `groups`, `memberOf`, and the OID in the SAML attribute consumer mapping. Pushing now.
deploy-bot: tenant=acme-poc-432 saml.attributeFallbacks updated: ["urn:oid:1.3.6.1.4.1.5923.1.1.1","groups","memberOf"] by nathan_enginfra
jamie_se: Also FYI, if they want SCIM to create groups we need to enable `scim.groupsEnabled` and grant `scim:groups` scope.
nathan_enginfra: Enabling group writes
deploy-bot: config update: tenant=acme-poc-432 key=scim.groupsEnabled old=false new=true
maya_sales: OK I'm coordinating: I'll ask ACME to switch the SCIM target, include X-Redwood-Tenant header, and retry user creation. Also will ask IdP admin to add groups claim or confirm claim name.
anita_security: One more ask from security questionnaire — they want to know whether SCIM payloads are logged in plaintext. Short answer: control plane logs redact PII, and customer audit logs can be enabled for the tenant. I'll DM the SOC runbook to team.
jamie_se: Perfect. If this all succeeds we can finalize Dedicated onboarding and start the performance tests. Fingers crossed for Friday demo :crossed_fingers:
maya_sales: Thanks everyone. I'll update thread when ACME confirms. Action items: nathan toggle strict -> done, add headers docs -> jamie to add short snippet to onboarding doc, anita to send SOC runbook. :thumbsup:
